newsitem.title: JAPAN: All months of Tokyo corn futures end higher.
newsitem.headline: All months of Tokyo corn futures end higher.

text.p: All months of Tokyo corn futures ended higher on Tuesday, as stronger CBOT Project A trading encouraged local investors to buy in the afternoon, local traders said.
Prices were 130 to 430 yen higher. The benchmark September 1997 contract was up 150 yen at 17,540 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 59,208 lots.
Nearby months rose sharply as active technical buying by individual investors emerged, the traders said.
Local traders said they would pay close attention to the USDA crop output report to be released on Wednesday.
The CBOT corn market surged when the USDA announced a lower-than-expected grain output forecast last month.
"We think it's safe to buy, given last month's experience," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot September contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.62-1/4 per bushel at 0820 GMT, against $3.62-1/4 at Monday's close.
The November of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.95-1/2 at 0820 GMT, against $7.93-3/4 from Monday's close.
